title: Streamline quant kernel API and scheduler integration
author: Anika Patel
description:
Motivation: This PR refactors the quantized kernel surface and plugs a lightweight hook into the scheduler to enable fused dequant+matmul execution for INT8 and FP8 code paths. Prior work introduced optimized kernels but left integration points ad-hoc; this change standardizes the kernel interface, exposes a scheduler hint API, and wires KV-cache alignment to continuous batching so that quantized requests can reuse prefix state safely.

What changed (high level):
- New stable kernel API (KernelAdapter) that normalizes tensor layout and quant metadata for all quant backends (INT8/FP8/smoothquant variants).
- Implemented a fused operator qmatmul_dequant_fused that performs dequant->matmul in a single pass for INT8 and FP8 variants. This reduces memory traffic and enables vectorized kernels on recent GPUs.
- Scheduler hint integration: added a lightweight Scheduler::PreferFusedQuant hook that the runtime uses when routing batched requests; hook is consulted during plan creation to co-locate compatible quant requests.
- KV cache alignment: continuous-batching now optionally aligns cached KV block boundaries for quantized runs to avoid misaligned dequant windows that previously forced expensive materialization. Controlled by config: quant.kv_align=true.
- Microbench harness and regression tests under tools/bench/quant_microbench to measure end-to-end latency and token throughput for representative LLaMA-variant sequences.
- Minor ergonomics: added runtime flag --quant-kernel=auto|fused|legacy and telemetry counters quant.fused_hits/fallbacks.

Checklist: 
- [x] Kernel API defined and unit-tested
- [x] Fused op implemented for INT8 and FP8 paths
- [x] Scheduler hint wired and validated with integration tests
- [x] KV cache alignment optional flag and tests
- [x] Benchmarks and perf CI added
- [x] Docs/example usage in redwood-examples/quantized_inference.md

Backwards compatibility and migration notes:
- Default behavior remains safe: legacy kernel mode preserved as --quant-kernel=legacy. The new fused path is enabled by default on recent CUDA builds detected at startup. If teams rely on exact byte-for-byte deterministic outputs, set --quant-kernel=legacy.
- No public API changes to the Redwood inference REST surface. This is purely serving-runtime implementation change.

Related: ENG-9832 has perf targets for INT8 cheap-dequant path; ENG-10021 tracks FP8 productionization. SUP-4123 surfaced customer incidents tied to quantized tail latency under high continuous-batching load.

review_comments: Marcus Liu: Nice consolidation. Question: will KernelAdapter introduce any allocation overhead on hot path? Please show a microbenchmark.
Author (Anika): Adapter uses preallocated scratch to avoid per-request allocs; added benchmark in tools/bench showing <1% overhead compared to inlined path for non-fused runs.
Diego Ramos: Scheduler hint looks good but what about multi-tenant isolation? Could fused-coalescing create noisy neighbor effects?

Author (Anika): Scheduler hint is advisory and only triggers when requests match quant metadata and customer tier allows co-location; added unit test to validate isolation policy respects tenant quotas.
Priya Singh: Please gate FP8 fused kernels behind feature detection on GPU driver/CUDA.
Author (Anika): Done — runtime checks CUDA version and device capability, falls back to legacy path if unsupported.
merge_details: Merged via squash on 2025-10-20 by Anika Patel. Commit message summarizes API change, fused operator and scheduler hook. Changelog entry added.
release_notes: Runtime: Added fused quantized dequant+matmul operator and scheduler integration for INT8/FP8. Expect 12-28% tail latency improvement for quantized workloads and reduced memory traffic. Feature enabled by default on modern CUDA-capable nodes; legacy mode available via --quant-kernel=legacy. See examples in redwood-examples/quantized_inference.md.
perf_results_summary: Microbench (A100, batch=1..8): INT8 fused path median token-latency -18% vs legacy, 95th -22%. FP8 fused path median -12%, 95th -15%. Throughput (tokens/s) up by 15% on steady-state batched runs when quant.kv_align=true. Memory peak reduced ~10% for fused runs. Perf CI tracks regression; this PR kept within expected bounds.
notes_for_ops: Ops should enable quant.kv_align in cluster config to get KV cache alignment benefits for continuous-batching. If encountering correctness mismatches with model outputs, toggle --quant-kernel=legacy and file SUP ticket.
